string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China and a municipality directly administered by the central government. Its urban history stretches back more than three thousand years, and it served as the capital of several imperial dynasties. The city combines historic neighbourhoods and monuments with modern universities, research institutions and transport networks. It is a national centre for politics, culture, international exchanges and scientific innovation. Visitors can explore its cultural heritage through museums, traditional streets and historic architecture. Beijing illustrates how an ancient capital continues to develop as a modern international city while preserving important connections to the past.

Shanghai is a municipality on the eastern coast of China, near the mouth of the Yangtze River. Its development reflects a long relationship with trade and water transport. Shanghai County was established in 1292, and the city opened as a treaty port in 1843. It later grew into an important commercial and industrial centre. Today, Shanghai is an international metropolis associated with finance, shipping, trade and innovation. Its sixteen districts include both densely developed urban neighbourhoods and outlying areas. The city brings together historical streets, modern business districts and diverse cultural traditions within the wider Yangtze River Delta region.

Chongqing is a municipality in southwestern China on the upper reaches of the Yangtze River. Its central urban area developed around the meeting of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers. Mountainous terrain, steep slopes and river valleys give the city its distinctive landscape and its reputation as the Mountain City. Chongqing became a municipality directly administered by the central government in 1997. Its territory includes large urban districts as well as agricultural areas and smaller towns. The region combines industry, commerce and transport with notable natural and cultural heritage, including the Dazu Rock Carvings and landscapes associated with the Three Gorges.

Tianjin is a municipality in northern China with a long history of commerce, industry and cultural exchange. Its official founding date is recorded as December 23, 1404, when a military garrison was established and the name Tianjin was adopted. In the modern period, the city became an important centre for foreign trade, finance and manufacturing in northern China. It was also associated with early developments in higher education, public health and postal services. Historic buildings and neighbourhoods reflect its encounters with different architectural traditions. Today, Tianjin continues to connect its historical identity with a diverse urban economy and cultural life.
